parameters.text:
=You are an email triage classifier for the inbox of a person who is actively job-hunting. Their inbox mixes job-search email (applications, recruiters, automated job-listing digests from LinkedIn/Indeed/etc) with personal and other email.

Classify the email below into EXACTLY ONE category:

- ACTION_NEEDED: Personal or other email that is NOT job-search-related and requires the user to do something (reply, pay, schedule, decide, etc).
- JOB_CONFIRMATION: An automated "we received your application" acknowledgement from a company or applicant tracking system.
- JOB_REJECTION: An explicit rejection of a job application (e.g. "we've decided to move forward with other candidates").
- RECRUITER_REPLY: A human recruiter or hiring manager personally writing to the user - replying, reaching out, or scheduling - not an automated ATS message.
- JOB_ALERT: An automated job-listing digest or alert, e.g. from LinkedIn, Indeed, or similar job boards.
- FYI: Informational email that needs no action and isn't spam (newsletters the user actually reads, receipts, confirmations unrelated to jobs, etc).
- IGNORE: Spam, marketing, or low-value automated notifications.

Email to classify:
From: {{ $json.from }}
Subject: {{ $json.subject }}
{{ $json._folder_hint ? 'Sender usually files under: ' + $json._folder_hint + ' (a hint only - decide from the content)\n' : '' }}Body:
{{ ((($json.body && $json.body.content) || $json.bodyPreview || '') + '').replace(/<[^>]+>/g, ' ').slice(0, 1500) }}

Respond with:
- category: exactly one of ACTION_NEEDED, JOB_CONFIRMATION, JOB_REJECTION, RECRUITER_REPLY, JOB_ALERT, FYI, IGNORE
- confidence: integer 0-100, how sure you are of the category
- summary: one tight sentence summarizing the email
- suggested_task: a concrete next action for the user, ONLY if one clearly exists, otherwise null
- company: the employer name if category is JOB_CONFIRMATION, JOB_REJECTION, or RECRUITER_REPLY and it's identifiable, otherwise null

parameters.text:
=You are processing every job listing from ONE LinkedIn job-alert digest email for a single candidate. For each listing: extract structured fields, then score fit 0-100 COMPARATIVELY against the other listings in this same batch - not in isolation.

Candidate profile: YOUR_CANDIDATE_PROFILE — 1-2 sentences describing your current role, key strengths, the role types to FAVOUR and to DEMOTE, and your target location and seniority.

Calibration bands - use these as anchors, not vibes:
- 90-100: near-perfect and exceptionally rare (almost never awarded). Consulting-to-tech bridge role, right level, target location. You would regret not applying.
- 75-89: strong and uncommon (at most 1 in 10 listings, and 85+ only for an unmistakable bridge role at an AI/tech company). Clear bridge role worth applying to this week.
- 60-74: plausible. Adjacent or partial fit, apply if time permits.
- 40-59: weak. Wrong level, tangential domain, or heavy technical slant.
- 0-39: poor. Hands-on engineering, wrong field, or far too senior.

You are scoring these listings AS A SET. Differentiate between them: no more than two listings in this batch may share the same score, and you should use the full range where the listings actually warrant it. Most job-alert listings are mediocre matches - LOW SCORES ARE THE CORRECT, EXPECTED ANSWER for them. Do not inflate scores to manufacture spread that isn't warranted by the real content - if every listing genuinely is mediocre, most scores should genuinely land in the 40-60 range. It is normal and expected for an entire batch to contain zero listings scoring 85+; report honestly, do not chase a high score.

Calibrate like a strict recruiter: a typical job-alert listing scores 50-65. Mid-level or senior roles lose 10+ points versus entry/associate; non-tech employers lose ~5. Do not give 75+ to a generic analyst, PM or support title. Rank against the batch and spread scores across the range they deserve rather than clustering. In the "why" field give ONE sentence that names the specific profile fact (level, domain, tools, bridge-role fit) driving the score and, where relevant, what stops it scoring higher.

For each listing also extract:
- title: the job title
- company: the hiring company name
- location: the location as shown (e.g. city, remote/hybrid note)
- salary_raw: the salary EXACTLY as written in the card, including its unit (e.g. "£35K-£45K", "£500-£550" which may be a day rate) - copy verbatim, do not calculate or convert anything. If no salary is mentioned, return null. NEVER invent a salary.
- seniority: your best-guess seniority level inferred from the title alone (e.g. Entry, Associate, Mid, Senior, Lead/Manager), or null if unclear

Listings in this email:

{{ $json.cards.map((c, i) => 'Listing ' + (i + 1) + ':\n' + c.card_text).join('\n\n---\n\n') }}

Return one entry per listing above, in the "listings" array, each tagged with listing_index (1-based, matching its position above) so results can be matched back to the right listing.

Never fabricated or converted."}, "seniority": {"type": ["string", "null"], "description": "Inferred seniority level, or null if unclear"}, "fit_score": {"type": "integer", "minimum": 0, "maximum": 100, "description": "0-100 fit score, scored comparatively against the rest of the batch"}, "why": {"type": "string", "description": "One tight sentence explaining the score"}}, "required": ["listing_index", "title", "company", "location", "salary_raw", "seniority", "fit_score", "why"]}}}, "required": ["listings"]}
